create.note: UWorldFactory, then the document's writable blocks applied under snapshot — `actors { }` creates by presence, `sublevels { }` restores what the map streams, and `level_blueprint { }` its script. A level takes NO `parent:`: a map is not an instance of a class, and its identity is the actors in it. **AND `actors { }` IS THE ONE BLOCK YOU USUALLY CANNOT PUT IN A CREATE DOCUMENT.** Snapshot means an omitted actor is DELETED, and a map is the one kind the factory does not hand you empty: the engine builds an `AWorldSettings` with it, one per level, which can be edited but never deleted. So a create document carrying `actors { }` is refused unless it names that actor — and it cannot: the name is minted when the map is made, so a created map's is bare `WorldSettings` while a map that has been round-tripped says `WorldSettings_1`, and copying either from an existing map's `.gc` gets it wrong. **THE ROUTE THAT WORKS IS TWO STEPS**: create with the header alone (blocks you leave out are not deleted — they keep whatever the factory gave the asset), read the projection back to learn that actor's name and its whole deviation list, then `gc_apply block:"actors"` carrying that line verbatim beside your own entries. Whether a create should apply `actors { }` as a patch instead is an open design question, not an oversight. `partition { }` is read BEFORE the factory runs and is the one block only the create can honour: it decides whether the new map is a World Partition map and whether streaming is on, and neither can be corrected once the world exists. Its ABSENCE means an ordinary map — so it overrides the project setting the factory would otherwise have used, and the document, not the machine running it, decides which map comes back. What a created map does not carry is derived rather than authored — collision_geometry, bsp_geometry, built_data, partition_hash, landscape_grid, foliage_instances — so it opens with no baked lighting and no built navmesh until something builds them, and any additive BSP the original had is not reproduced (no map in this project has any). Volumes DO come back with their shape: the builder is authored and the model is rebuilt from it.

blocks.name: partition
blocks.note: Whether this map is a World Partition map, and it is the ONE fact about a level that cannot be fixed after the fact. Two keys, no entries. `streaming: enabled|disabled` — its PRESENCE says the world has a UWorldPartition and its value is that partition's bEnableStreaming, so one key carries both and neither is written twice. `external_actors: true` is ULevel's own OFPA flag, for a PLAIN level with Use External Actors ticked; it is refused beside `streaming:` because a partitioned world has it forced true by the engine, which makes it derived there rather than authored. An unknown key is refused rather than ignored. WRITTEN ONLY BY CREATE. A world picks its partition backend when it is built — UWorld::InitializeNewWorld is the only door — so gc_apply create:true hands these to UWorldFactory, and an apply onto an EXISTING map VERIFIES instead: matching, it does nothing; disagreeing, it refuses and names both sides. That refusal is the whole point of the block. Before it, a created level was partitioned or not according to the PROJECT SETTINGS of whoever ran the apply, with nothing in the file or the result saying which. WHAT IT DOES NOT CARRY is the runtime hash — the grids, the cell sizes, the loading ranges and the HLOD setups — declared in omits: as 'partition_hash'. UE 5.7 ships two unrelated hash shapes and a grammar fitted to one covers one, so this pass declares the gap rather than half-closing it. Data layers are not here either; they are their own row.

blocks.name: actors
blocks.note: Create is by PRESENCE — an entry naming no live actor spawns one. Under the default omission:"patch" a delete needs an explicit `delete <Name>` line and never omission, because the referencer walk cannot see into the Level Blueprint, so the document cannot show you what a deletion costs. Under omission:"snapshot" the block IS the complete actor list, so an omitted actor is deleted and a `delete` line is refused as a contradiction — the referencer gate and its allow_breaking_changes are unchanged either way.

blocks.name: objects
blocks.note: Every NON-ACTOR object this level's document references, declared ONCE — `<Actor>.<Object> = <ClassPath>(<changed fields>)`. It is the third block to take a value out of an actor entry and leave a reference behind, after volumes{} and splines{}, and the first where the thing moved can be reached from MORE THAN ONE entry: a BP_Surface outered to BP_Wall_C_5 is also pointed at by BP_ItemManager_C_2 and by four BP_FloorCeilings, so inlining it at every site would write one object's fields once per pointer. Declaring it here makes the entries say obj'…' and this block say what the object is. THE HANDLE IS THE NAME because the engine's reference is: a .umap stores an object pointer as an export index and there is no GUID on a sub-object, so an object whose name changes is a different object — actors{}'s own ruling for a rename. ONLY THE CHANGED FIELDS, against the object's archetype, which is what baseline: archetype already means everywhere else in the file; an inline instanced(…) body still writes defaults and cannot stop, because documents that state them are already committed. CREATE BY PRESENCE and NO DELETE: an entry naming no live object creates it under the outer its handle names, and an object this block does not name is one whose state is unchanged under patch and snapshot alike — removing one means clearing the field that points at it, which is a line in actors{}, where the referencer gate is. AN ENTRY IS A WHOLE VALUE, so a field it omits ends at the archetype. THE OUTER MUST EXIST: a handle is rooted at an actor's document name, so on a level being rebuilt actors{} is applied first. NOT CARRIED are components, which the actor entry's own braces declare, and any object outered straight to the ULevel or the UWorld rather than below an actor — no entry could ever have inlined those, so declaring them would invent state rather than move it. TWO MORE STAY WHERE THEY WERE. A declared UPROPERTY(Instanced) value is still written INLINE: the class author has stated exclusive ownership, so the entry is already its one declaration site — and hoisting ABrush::BrushBuilder moved a brush's extent off the actor line, where RebuildBrushShape is the only thing that reads it, so an edited shape wrote a new builder and kept the old polygons. A TRANSIENT object (RF_Transient or RF_TextExportTransient) is not declared at all, the same guard a transient ACTOR gets and for the same reason: it is not in the .umap this sidecar binds to, and a .gc is itself a text export. The live case is a dynamic material instance, which is created transient and which one measured level holds 35 of.

blocks.name: sublevels
blocks.note: How this level streams other maps — one entry per streaming level, named by the PACKAGE it streams, carrying the ULevelStreaming class, LevelTransform and the initially-loaded/visible flags. Never what is inside a sublevel: that is its own .umap with its own .gc, and an entry with a body is refused by name. The lifecycle is the actors block's, because they are one document — create by PRESENCE, remove by an explicit `delete <Package>` under the default omission:"patch", and under omission:"snapshot" the block IS the complete set so an omitted entry is removed and a `delete` line is refused. One place it is wider than actors: a class change is carried, because SetStreamingClassForLevel is the Levels panel's own Change Streaming Method and it carries the settings across, where an actor's class change has no equivalent. A package that does not exist is refused — this block streams a map, it does not author one. Absent entirely on a level that streams nothing, and on a World Partition level, which builds runtime cells from a grid instead of authoring streaming levels.

blocks.name: volumes
blocks.note: A brush's actual geometry, for a brush its BrushBuilder no longer describes. ONE LINE PER BRUSH, named by the same document name the actors block uses, and in ONE OF TWO FORMS — the same `Name = value(…)` entry shape actors{} and sublevels{} already use. `<Name> = moved(i x y z, i x y z, …)` where the brush still has a builder and somebody dragged it: the base is that builder, on this actor's own line in this same document, and the entry states only the corners that left it — a one-corner drag on a 64-point disc is 36 characters against 6,271, because a delta's cost scales with the EDIT and not with the shape. `<Name> = points(x y z, …) faces(i j k, …)` where nothing describes the shape at all, or where so much moved that the delta is no longer the shorter of the two; it also takes over whenever the edit is not corners moving — a face added or removed, a ring re-wound, corners split or merged — because a delta cannot say any of those. An entry that is both forms, or neither, is refused by name. Points are unnamed and ordered, because nothing references them and named ones would renumber the whole entry on an insert. The form is INDEXED rather than a flat polygon list because the engine's flat emit repeats every position about five times; no Base, Normal, TextureU or TextureV is written, because FPoly::Finalize derives all four and storing them costs +291-347%. A `moved(…)` entry is resolved back into a whole shape against the actor's builder BEFORE anything is written, so both forms take one apply path; a delta whose corner the builder does not have is refused whole rather than half-applied, because the builder has changed since it was recorded. ABSENT unless a level holds such a brush — one whose builder still describes it carries its shape as that builder's parameters in its actors{} entry instead, and writing both would be two carriers of one fact. OMISSION NEVER CLEARS GEOMETRY, under patch and snapshot alike: a brush this block does not name is one whose shape is unchanged, and clearing it would destroy a solid no file records. There is no `delete` token and no create — an entry naming no live actor is refused, because spawning a brush from geometry alone would invent an actor with no class and no transform, and an entry with no faces is refused because it would leave a brush with no solid at all. The apply writes the polygons and THEN runs the CSG pass, because a volume's collision comes from its Nodes and not from its polygons — without it the brush would draw the new shape and still CONTAIN the old one. Applying a block that matches what is already there writes nothing and dirties nothing.

blocks.name: splines
blocks.note: A spline component's CURVE, moved out of the actor entry into a named block at the bottom of the level. ONE LINE PER SPLINE, named `<Actor>.<Component>` — one token longer than volumes{}'s handle because a brush IS its actor's shape while one actor may carry several splines — and the component's own entry keeps the name: `Course = WaterSplineComponent(SplineCurves=$Brook.Course)`. `<Name> = points(x y z, …) modes(<one word>)`, with optional arrive(…) and leave(…) clauses. WHY IT MOVED: USplineComponent::SplineCurves is UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere), so the reflective walk inlined the whole struct — one plain 20-point spline actor was 14,055 characters of actors block, and is now 1,020 plus a 428-character entry. NEARLY ALL OF THAT WAS DATA NOBODY AUTHORED, and two derived things ride inside that EditAnywhere struct: ReparamTable, a distance-to-parameter cache UpdateSpline rebuilds wholesale and 39.5% of the old block; and ArriveTangent/LeaveTangent on any AUTO point, which AutoSetTangents recomputes — storing those is storing an output, and storing a stale one is worse, because an apply writes tangents the curve overwrites on its next update. A curveuser or curvebreak point DOES carry its tangents and a spec pins that, so the saving never becomes a silent flattening of a hand-tuned curve. EVERY OPTIONAL CLAUSE IS ABSENT WHEN IT WOULD SAY NOTHING, and the absence is load-bearing: no arrive(…) means these tangents are COMPUTED, which is a different claim from these tangents are zero. modes(<one word>) means every point, because a hand-drawn spline is curveauto throughout. NO CREATE, NO DELETE and no mode branch — volumes{}'s rulings unchanged: an entry names a component the actors block already declares, and omission means this curve is UNCHANGED under patch and snapshot alike. THE GATE IS THE CURVE AND NOT THE TEXT: a spline's usable output is GetLocationAtDistanceAlongSpline, which reads the very tangents and reparam table this block omits, so Rebuild ends with UpdateSpline() and the ordering lives in the codec rather than in each caller. THE EXCLUSION IS A DELEGATE AND NOT A RULE ABOUT THE COMPONENT CLASS: only a document that HAS a splines{} block may leave the curve out, so a level does and an Actor Blueprint's components{} and a .gcp capture do NOT — they still inline their curves, reparam table and all, because excluding the field there would delete a curve with nowhere to put it.

blocks.name: data_layers
blocks.note: The world's DATA LAYER TREE, on the AWorldDataLayers actor that owns it — which layer instances the map has, their hierarchy, and their initial editor and runtime state. World Partition row 6. It exists because nothing else reached it: AWorldDataLayers::DataLayerInstances is UPROPERTY() with NO EditAnywhere, since layers are edited in the Data Layers outliner rather than a details panel, so the visibility rule dropped the set whole and the actor's document read 'WorldDataLayers = /Script/Engine.WorldDataLayers()' — empty parens — however many layers the map held. TWO OF THIS SUBJECT'S THREE CARRIERS NEEDED NOTHING BUILT and are worth knowing so you do not go looking for a block that does not exist: the LAYER ITSELF is a UDataLayerAsset, a UDataAsset whose authored fields are all EditAnywhere, so it already projects whole as kind:data_asset — ask for that kind, there is no kind:data_layer. And which layers an ACTOR belongs to is AActor::DataLayerAssets, UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, AdvancedDisplay), so it is already an ordinary property line in that actor's own entry and it already applies back; there is no membership directive to write. ONE ENTRY PER LAYER INSTANCE, named by the PACKAGE of the asset behind it, carrying the UDataLayerInstance class on the line with the deviations bundled after it — the `Name = value(…)` entry shape actors{} and sublevels{} already use. Named by the ASSET and never by the instance for a measured reason: UDataLayerInstanceWithAsset::MakeName is 'DataLayer_' plus a FRESH FGuid, so the instance's own name is a digest that changes every time a layer is recreated. Parent= is the one synthesised key and it names the parent's asset package too, so a reference reads the same as the entry it points at; the engine's own Parent pointer is UPROPERTY() with no EditAnywhere and would print that GUID name. ABSENT ENTIRELY on a map with no data layers, which is most maps and every non-partitioned one — absence means none, not a dropped block. READ-ONLY for now: the tree is projected and not yet applied.

blocks.name: settings
blocks.note: Asset-wide LOD and interpolation, as deviations from Unreal's default Groom: LODMode (Default follows the project, Manual uses each group's lods, Auto ignores them), AutoLODBias, EnableGlobalInterpolation, EnableSimulationCache, HairInterpolationType, MinLOD, DisableBelowMinLodStripping. patch sets what it names and `reset <Path>` returns one; snapshot is the whole set.

blocks.name: groups
blocks.note: Named source/guide counts, derived maximum length and resolved material per Hair Group. Generated curves and recipe-owned strand materials are edited in `.gcgroom`, not here.

blocks.name: group_materials
blocks.note: The Groom's named native material slots, one `SlotName = obj'/Path/Material.Material'` line each. Add a separate slot for a card atlas, then name it in cards.MaterialSlotName. patch carries every existing slot and uses `delete <SlotName>` for an unused slot; snapshot is the complete slot set. A `.gcgroom` recipe still owns the strand slot named after each of its groups, while additional card or mesh slots survive recipe rebuilds.

blocks.name: rendering
blocks.note: Each Hair Group's rendering settings (geometry, shadow, advanced), one `Name = group(...)` line per group, keyed by the group's NAME and never its position; the line is the group's whole value, as deviations from Unreal's default. patch carries every group and `reset <Name>` returns one to the default; under snapshot a group left out returns to it. On a Groom a `.gcgroom` built, MaterialSlotName is the recipe's.

blocks.name: physics
blocks.note: Each Hair Group's simulation: solver (SolverSettings.EnableSimulation), external forces, material, collisions and strands, `Name = group(...)` per group as in `rendering`. A group a `.gcgroom` builds starts with simulation off; what is written here survives its rebuilds.

blocks.name: interpolation
blocks.note: Each Hair Group's decimation and guide interpolation, `Name = group(...)` per group as in `rendering`. InterpolationSettings.bUseUniqueGuide makes each hair follow a single guide. On a group whose guides a `.gcgroom` placed (GuideType Imported), GuideType is the recipe's.

blocks.name: lods
blocks.note: Each Hair Group's LOD list, `Name = group(LODs=...)` per group as in `rendering`: per LOD the curve and vertex decimation, screen size, thickness, visibility, geometry (Strands, Cards or Meshes) and whether it simulates. Ignored while `settings` LODMode resolves to Auto.

blocks.name: cards
blocks.note: What each Hair Group draws at a LOD whose GeometryType is Cards, `Name = group(HairGroupsCards=(...))` per group as in `rendering`: one entry per LOD -- LODIndex, the card mesh (ImportedMesh), its texture layout and textures, GuideType and MaterialSlotName. Unreal draws the first entry for a LOD; LODIndex -1 is not used, and an entry that sets nothing is Unreal's empty slot and is not shown. GroupIndex is the line's name and is never written.

blocks.name: meshes
blocks.note: What each Hair Group draws at a LOD whose GeometryType is Meshes, `Name = group(HairGroupsMeshes=(...))` per group, entries as in `cards`: LODIndex, ImportedMesh, textures and MaterialSlotName.

blocks.name: settings
blocks.note: Editable native Control Rig properties. Patch preserves absent values; snapshot returns absent values to class defaults. PreviewSkeletalMesh in a create recipe seeds bones and calibrated controls from a .gcrig-prepared character.

blocks.name: rig
blocks.note: Prepared .gcrig setup: source, skeleton, spaces, axes, chains, limits and calibration. Managed regeneration updates source context and retains prior setup under authored.FunctionName for preserved function bodies.

blocks.name: hierarchy
blocks.note: One line per element, parents before children and siblings by name: `<type> <name> [parent=…, location=…, offset_location=…, shape_scale=…, …]`. The eight types are bone, null, control, curve, physics, reference, connector and socket. Transforms are stated INITIAL and LOCAL and only where they deviate from identity — current transforms are whatever the last evaluation left behind and are not asset state. A CONTROL IS THREE TRANSFORMS and all three are carried: its own local one, the `offset_` frame that value is measured against, and the `shape_` transform its gizmo is drawn with. `parent=` is a KEY (`bone:pelvis`) and not a bare name, because two elements of different types may share one. An element with more than one parent — a space-switched control — states the first and reports the rest as UNSUPPORTED.

blocks.name: properties
blocks.write_condition: native RigVM statement types; unsupported content is preserved by patch and prevents snapshot replacement
blocks.note: Members use properties { Name: Type = Default [instance_editable] }. Functions use input{}, output{}, io{}, local declarations and [mutable]. Nodes use Type(Pin=Value, Pin=Node.Pin) : ->Next, with off-pin properties in [] and resolved types in !types[]. Patch preserves absent members/nodes; delete Name removes one in its block. Snapshot replaces supplied blocks. Coupled properties and graph compile together on a private candidate. Generated functions follow upstream .gcrig override:true|false; unrelated functions and solve wiring survive regeneration.

create.refusal: an import document describes an asset that does not exist yet and names the source file that would make it. Creating it is `gc_import`, which is a different operation with a different gate, not a restore.

recoverable_remove.refusal: an import document is a plan, not an asset. There is no package to move and nothing to recover.

blocks.name: import
blocks.note: The source and its hash. `source_hash` is the staleness guard rather than `sig:`, because the body is MEANT to be edited between the plan and the import. `source` may name an ARCHIVE — a .zip, .7z, .tar or a compressed tar — and then it is the archive's hash that guards the pair of calls.

blocks.name: pipelines
blocks.note: Read from the project's own Interchange pipeline stack and its class defaults, so it cannot drift from what the editor does. Present only where Interchange claims the source format; `factory` is the other engine and a document carrying both is refused.

blocks.name: settings
blocks.note: What the imported ASSET becomes, as opposed to how the file is read — `CompressionSettings`, `SRGB`, `MipGenSettings`. It is the same block and the same writer `kind:texture_2d` uses, so every name spelled here reads back in the sidecar. Offered only for a TEXTURE-ONLY source, because one settings block cannot name a mesh and its three textures, and applied as a PATCH: a proposal naming nothing did not ask to lose what the pipeline chose. `GC-IMPORT-DESIGN.md` §5.

blocks.name: factory
blocks.note: The editor's own `UFactory` for a format Interchange does not claim — audio is the usual case, because a stock build ships every Interchange audio flag off. One entry, rule 7, carrying the factory's `EditAnywhere` settings as deviations from its CDO. Its `Formats` and `SupportedClass` are NOT editable: they are how a factory is found rather than anything a caller decides. `GC-IMPORT-DESIGN.md` §8.

blocks.name: members
blocks.note: Every file inside an ARCHIVE source this build can import, one quoted path per line — the whole batch in one document, because a pack's meshes share one set of settings and a document per member would be that decision copied 192 times. Narrow it by DELETING lines; nothing absent from the block can be imported by it. There is no `= destination` form: the archive's own folder tree is what decides where each member lands, mirrored under the destination folder. Members that do not all import the same way are refused by name. `GC-IMPORT-DESIGN.md` §7.

blocks.name: settings
blocks.note: The graph's own reflective fields as value assignments (`Name = Value`), as deviations from a fresh UPCGGraph — hierarchical generation and its grid, the landscape flags, the cooking and standalone flags. An untouched graph writes an empty block rather than a roll call of engine defaults. The node list, the two terminals, the comment boxes and the parameter bag are each a block of their own and are excluded here. WRITING: the payload is imported onto a scratch graph and re-projected before the asset is touched, so a value that would not read back as it was written is refused rather than partly applied. Stating a value that EQUALS the default is accepted and then stops being printed, because a deviations block spells the default by saying nothing.

blocks.name: parameters
blocks.note: `UserParameters` — the graph's PUBLIC API — as `Name: type = value`, one line per declared parameter. A DECLARATION list, not a deviation list: every parameter appears whether or not its value differs from its type's zero, because the parameter existing is the authored fact and a graph instance overrides it by this name. The `= value` half is the deviation, so `Density: double` means declared and left at zero. A parameter is read by a `GetGraphParameter` node in `graph { }` and wired like any other pin — there is no parameter reference inside a property value, because the engine has no such binding.

blocks.name: graph
blocks.note: The nodes, as `alias = Type(pins) [props]`, with the two terminals named `input` and `output` and the rest `n0..nk` in the graph's stored order. THE PINS ARE NAMED, NOT INDEXED (`In=n1.Out`), because PCG addresses pins by FName label everywhere and a label is unique per node per direction; a label containing a space is backtick-quoted. Only CONNECTED input pins are written — a node's pin set is computed from its settings, so a document never asserts pins — and one pin taking several edges is a bundle (`In=(n1.Out, n2.Out)`). Props are `EditAnywhere` deviations from the settings class CDO; a series or a contained sub-object opens a `{ }` body instead, on a structural test rather than a width threshold. A node whose settings are a shared asset writes `[settings=obj'…']` and NO inline props; a subgraph node writes `[graph=obj'…']` and is never inlined, carrying an `overrides { Name = Value }` body for whatever THIS call site changed about the child. A node's comment bubble is a `//` line immediately above its statement, which is `behaviortree { }`'s spelling — a comment BOX spans nodes and is a statement in `comments { }`, a BUBBLE hangs off one node and is prose. WRITING: the payload is the whole graph — a node it omits is removed, and each removal is named. A node whose alias and class both still match is REUSED, so applying a projection back changes nothing; a node this write creates is placed below the existing rows, because positions are not in this document and where a node sits is what `comments { }` derives its membership from. The write is performed on a copy and re-projected before the asset is touched.

blocks.name: comments
blocks.note: The editor's comment boxes, each carrying its text, its colour when it is not white, and `covers=` — the aliases of the nodes it encloses. The RECTANGLE is not written: which nodes an author drew a box around is the fact, and deriving the geometry from the membership is what lets `omits: node_layout` be honest about positions. Coverage is a node's origin inside the box, because a node's width is a Slate measurement that does not exist outside an open editor.

blocks.name: settings
blocks.note: The reflective half: `Skeleton` (what a create reads), `RateScale`, `bLoop`, `PreviewBasePose` and the rest of the shared `UAnimSequenceBase` settings. Excluded: the track (its own block) and the derived `CommonTargetFrameRate`. An omitted property REFUSES and `reset <Path>` returns one to its default.

blocks.name: track
blocks.note: What the composite plays, in order: `segment(Animation=obj'…', StartPos=…, AnimStartTime=…, AnimEndTime=…, AnimPlayRate=…, LoopingCount=…)`, the montage slot's segment spelling. Segments have no names, so the list IS the value: snapshot only, rebuilt whole. `Animation=` is required per segment. Refused: an animation on another skeleton, one the engine's `IsValidToAdd` rejects, a segment that plays no frames, and the composite itself (directly or through a composite it plays). The length is the engine's, recomputed from the track.

blocks.name: curves
blocks.note: Float curves, `<name> = FloatCurve(…, keys=…)`, KEYED BY NAME — the one list on this asset that has a real key, because a curve name is how an anim graph, a material and Blueprint all reach one. Keys go through the project's single curve-key spelling; a duplicated name is reported and neither curve is written. Read through `GetCurveData()`, since the member is deprecated and protected. Transform curves are `omits: transform_curves`. Written through `IAnimationDataController` for the same reason, one call per authored field — `SetCurveKeys` writes keys and nothing else, so the extrapolation goes through `SetCurveAttributes` beside it. `delete <Name>` and `rename <Old> -> <New>`; an omitted curve refuses under patch and IS the deletion under snapshot.

blocks.name: notify_tracks
blocks.note: The notify editor's lanes, `track(TrackName=…, TrackColor=…)`, ORDERED AND ANONYMOUS: a notify names its lane by index and lane names are not unique — the engine's defaults are `1`, `2`, `3`. Declared before `notifies` because this is the vocabulary and that is the usage — and APPLIED before it too, for the same reason the order is not a preference: a notify names its lane by index. TRUNCATES, `snapshot` only. A payload may not empty the list and may not leave a lane a live notify names.

blocks.name: notifies
blocks.note: The timed events, in the engine's own time order, as anonymous statements: `notify(…)` for an instant and `notify_state(…)` for a span. NO KEY — a notify's only stable handle is a `Guid` the engine marks `ExcludeFromHash`, and two notifies may share a name. `Time=` comes from `GetTime()` and is always stated; the anchor's raw members are the montage-linking half and are not carried. The notify class arrives inside its `instanced(…)` value. TRUNCATES, `snapshot` only: a written notify is a NEW notify, because its class is an instanced sub-object, its anchor is protected and its Guid is minted by the engine.

create.note: UNiagaraSimCacheFactoryNew makes the empty cache; `capture { }` then records the system into it, synchronously, in a private world. A long capture: gc_apply wait:0 and collect it with unreal_info include:["tasks"].

blocks.name: capture
blocks.note: The recipe that records the cache: System (obj'…' to a Niagara system), Seconds (simulated time, up to 120) and FrameRate (frames per simulated second, 1 to 240), then the engine's FNiagaraSimCacheCreateParameters as deviations (AttributeCaptureMode = All, RenderingOnly or ExplicitAttributes with ExplicitCaptureAttributes = ("<Emitter>.Particles.<Attribute>", …), bAllowInterpolation, …). Writing it records the system again in a private world, replacing every frame; a recipe equal to the recording records nothing. Patch keeps an unstated field and `reset <Name>` returns it to its default; snapshot reads the payload as the whole recipe.

blocks.name: frames
blocks.note: What the recording holds over time: Count (frames), StartSeconds (the system's age at the first frame), DurationSeconds (first to last frame) and PeakParticles.<Emitter> (the most particles that emitter held in any frame).

blocks.name: system
blocks.note: The system-level attributes each frame holds, `Name: Type`, then any data interface whose data the cache stored, marked [stored].

entry_specifiers.sets: this line is a data interface whose per-frame data the cache stored (bAllowDataInterfaceCaching), not a system attribute
entry_specifiers.default: absent — the line is a system attribute the frames hold

blocks.name: emitters
blocks.note: One `Name = emitter(props) { }` per recorded emitter, props spelled as niagara_system's (SimTarget, LocalSpace, written only when not the default), holding each recorded particle attribute as `Particles.<Name>: Type`. A disabled or stateless emitter records nothing and is absent.
